points.point: BOJ ended negative interest rates, saying the policy had fulfilled its role
points.quote: The Bank considers that the policy framework of Quantitative and Qualitative Monetary Easing (QQE) with Yield Curve Control and the negative interest rate policy to date have fulfilled their roles.
paraphrases: The BOJ ended negative interest rates, saying the policy had fulfilled its role.
BOJ scrapped NIRP, its first rate hike since 2007.
The Bank of Japan declared its negative-rate policy had done its job and would end.
decoys: The BOJ said it would maintain negative rates for the foreseeable future.
The BOJ ended its ETF purchase program, calling it a success.

points.point: BOJ ended yield curve control (YCC), saying the framework had fulfilled its role
points.quote: The Bank considers that the policy framework of Quantitative and Qualitative Monetary Easing (QQE) with Yield Curve Control and the negative interest rate policy to date have fulfilled their roles.
paraphrases: The BOJ ended yield curve control, saying the framework had fulfilled its role.
BOJ scrapped YCC as part of the policy overhaul.
The Bank of Japan declared its YCC framework had done its job and would end.
decoys: The BOJ said yield curve control would remain a core tool for policy for years to come.
The BOJ tightened its yield curve control band rather than removing it.

points.point: BOJ set a new guideline of 0 to 0.1 percent for the overnight call rate, its first hike since 2007
points.quote: The Bank will encourage the uncollateralized overnight call rate to remain at around 0 to 0.1 percent.
paraphrases: BOJ set a new call rate guideline of 0 to 0.1 percent, its first hike in 17 years.
The Bank raised short-term rates to a range of 0-0.1%, ending eight years of NIRP.
New guideline: overnight call rate at 0 to 0.10 percent.
decoys: BOJ set the new guideline at 0.1 to 0.25 percent.
BOJ kept the call rate at -0.1 percent, unchanged.

points.point: Nakamura Toyoaki dissented against ending the framework
points.quote: V oting against the action: NAKAMURA Toyoaki and NOGUCHI Asahi.
paraphrases: Nakamura Toyoaki dissented from ending negative rates.
Board member Nakamura voted against the policy framework change.
Nakamura dissented, wanting to keep negative rates until smaller firms could raise wages.
decoys: Nakamura supported ending NIRP immediately, ahead of other members.
Governor Ueda dissented, preferring to keep rates negative.

points.point: Noguchi Asahi dissented against ending the framework
points.quote: V oting against the action: NAKAMURA Toyoaki and NOGUCHI Asahi.
paraphrases: Noguchi Asahi dissented from ending negative rates.
Board member Noguchi voted against the policy framework change.
Noguchi dissented, arguing the BOJ should avoid discontinuous changes in financial conditions.
decoys: Noguchi supported ending NIRP immediately, ahead of other members.
Governor Ueda dissented, preferring to keep rates negative.

points.point: BOJ will discontinue ETF and J-REIT purchases
points.quote: The Bank will discontinue purchases of exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and Japan real estate investment trusts (J-REITs).
paraphrases: The BOJ will stop buying ETFs and J-REITs altogether.
BOJ to discontinue purchases of exchange-traded funds and Japanese REITs.
The Bank will halt ETF and J-REIT purchases as part of the policy overhaul.
decoys: The BOJ will continue ETF purchases at a reduced pace.
The BOJ will discontinue JGB purchases entirely.

points.point: BOJ will gradually reduce and discontinue CP and corporate bond purchases within about a year
points.quote: The Bank will gradually reduce the amount of purchases of CP and corporate bonds and will discontinue the purchases in about one year.
paraphrases: The BOJ will gradually reduce CP and corporate bond purchases and end them within about a year.
Purchases of commercial paper and corporate bonds will be phased out over roughly one year.
The Bank will wind down its CP and corporate bond buying, discontinuing it in about a year.
decoys: The BOJ will immediately halt all CP and corporate bond purchases.
The BOJ will continue CP and corporate bond purchases indefinitely at the current pace.

points.point: BOJ judged the wage-price virtuous cycle had become more solid
points.quote: the virtuous cycle between wages and prices has become more solid
paraphrases: The BOJ judged the virtuous cycle between wages and prices had become more solid.
The Bank concluded the wage-price virtuous cycle was solid enough to end easing.
BOJ said the wage-price virtuous cycle had strengthened and become more solid.
decoys: The BOJ said the wage-price cycle remained too weak to justify a hike.
The BOJ said the virtuous cycle had weakened over the past year.

points.point: BOJ judged the 2% price target now in sight of being achieved sustainably
points.quote: judged it came in sight that the price stability target of 2 percent would be achieved in a sustainable and stable manner
paraphrases: BOJ said the 2% price target is now in sight of being achieved sustainably.
The Bank judged that sustainable, stable achievement of its 2% goal had come into view.
BOJ concluded the 2 percent inflation target could now be reached in a sustainable and stable manner.
decoys: The BOJ said the 2% target was unlikely to be reached for years.
The BOJ said achieving 2% inflation sustainably remained a distant prospect.

points.point: BOJ will continue JGB purchases at broadly the same pace as before
points.quote: The Bank will continue its JGB purchases with broadly the same amount as before.
paraphrases: The BOJ will keep buying JGBs at broadly the same pace as before.
JGB purchases continue unchanged, the BOJ said.
The Bank left its bond-buying pace steady, broadly matching the prior amount.
decoys: The BOJ will cut JGB purchases in half compared with before.
The BOJ will end all JGB purchases immediately.

points.point: BOJ's JGB purchases are currently about 6 trillion yen per month
points.quote: The amount of JGB purchases is curr ently about 6 trillion yen per month.
paraphrases: JGB purchases currently run about 6 trillion yen per month.
The BOJ's bond-buying pace is roughly ¥6tn monthly.
About 6 trillion yen a month in JGBs are being purchased, the BOJ noted.
decoys: JGB purchases currently run about 3 trillion yen per month.
JGB purchases currently run about 9 trillion yen per month.

points.point: Wages are expected to continue increasing steadily this year, following firm spring wage negotiations
points.quote: it is highly likely that wages will continue to increase steadily this year, following the firm wage increase last year
paraphrases: Wages are expected to keep rising steadily this year, following firm gains last year.
The BOJ noted strong spring wage negotiation results pointing to steady pay growth.
Firms are expected to continue raising wages steadily, per this year's shunto results.
decoys: Wage growth is expected to stagnate this year after last year's gains.
The BOJ said price growth, not wages, would drive the outlook.
